lesson.headline: JLPT N2 (Pre-Advanced) — Compound Particles & Media Grammar
lesson.lead: Expanding literacy to comprehend newspapers, journals, and broadcast television. Mastering compound connectors, social boundaries, and developing trends.
bullets: Compound Particles: に 対して (ni taishite - in contrast to / regarding), に 伴って (ni tomonatte - along with / in parallel with).
Social and Moral Norms: 〜わけにはいかない (wake ni wa ikanai - cannot afford to do under social norms or moral obligation).
Continuous Trends: 〜つつある (tsutsu aru - in the process of / currently developing, e.g. "the population is decreasing").
Physical tendencies: 〜がちだ (gachi da - tendency to happen frequently, usually with negative outcomes, e.g. "tendency to forget").

quizzes.q: Which N2 grammar pattern translates to "cannot afford to do" due to moral, social or corporate expectations?
options: わけにはいかない (wake ni wa ikanai)
ことにしている (koto ni shite iru)
quizzes.explain: 〜わけにはいかない (wake ni wa ikanai) indicates that while you physically could perform the action, social codes or moral rules prevent you from doing so.

quizzes.q: Complete: "The temperature is in the process of dropping" (気温が下がり___).
quizzes.explain: 〜つつある (tsutsu aru) is a formal, written expression used to show an ongoing trend or process: "is in the process of dropping".

quizzes.q: What is the meaning of the N2 compound particle "〜にともなって" (ni tomonatte)?
options: Along with / as a result of
quizzes.explain: 〜に伴って (ni tomonatte) means "along with", "in proportion to", or "as a result of", indicating that one change triggers another in parallel.

quizzes.q: What is the correct reading of the N2 pre-advanced Kanji compound "環境" (environment)?
quizzes.explain: 環境 is read as "かんきょう" (kankyou), combining 環 (ring/circle/surroundings) and 境 (boundary/border).

quizzes.q: What does "〜気味" (gimi) indicate when added to a noun (e.g. 風邪気味 - kaze-gimi)?
options: A slight feeling or tendency of
quizzes.explain: 〜気味 (gimi) denotes a slight physical or mental tendency of a state, usually negative: "a touch of / slight feeling of". E.g. 風邪気味 (a touch of a cold).

quizzes.q: Which N2 grammar connector represents "simply because of / as a result of" (expressing regret or an unexpected negative outcome)?
quizzes.explain: 〜ばかりに (bakari ni) means "simply because of / solely due to," highlighting that a single factor caused an unfortunate or regrettable result.
